answer: Latency triangulation: each agent must echo signed nonces from three verifiers picked at random on different continents. Round-trip times fix where it physically runs, like plotting an orchard row on a map. Identities whose timing fingerprints match within 2 ms are merged as one host and flagged violet. To keep 1,000 fakes alive an attacker must rent ~1,000 servers in separate cities, about $5 each a month, while a fake earns well under $1. Nonces rotate daily, so replies can't be replayed, and an ivory-tower rack of clones fails at once.
